Integration with crywolf: clip manifest and validation tables

Source: vignettes/crywolf-integration.Rmd
crywolf-integration.Rmd

sheepdog writes two tables that occupancy models with false positives, such as those of the crywolf package, read: clip_manifest.csv (extract_validation_clips()) and validation_by_clip.csv (post_validation()). This document fixes their columns, types and the definition of an occasion. The two packages are independent: sheepdog does not depend on crywolf, and crywolf reads these files without loading sheepdog.

Example files ship with the package:

library(sheepdog)
manifest   <- system.file("extdata", "clip_manifest.csv", package = "sheepdog")
validation <- system.file("extdata", "validation_by_clip.csv",
                          package = "sheepdog")
v <- readr::read_csv(validation, show_col_types = FALSE)
v[, c("site", "occasion_id", "confidence", "n_detections_occasion",
      "inclusion_prob", "verdict")]
#> # A tibble: 12 × 6
#>    site  occasion_id     confidence n_detections_occasion inclusion_prob verdict
#>    <chr> <chr>                <dbl>                 <dbl>          <dbl> <chr>  
#>  1 ARA   ARA01_20220110…      0.913                     1          0.25  positi…
#>  2 ARA   ARA01_20220110…      0.789                     2          0.25  positi…
#>  3 ARA   ARA01_20220110…      0.938                     2          0.25  positi…
#>  4 ARA   ARA01_20220111…      0.532                     3          0.25  negati…
#>  5 ARA   ARA01_20220111…      0.699                     3          0.25  negati…
#>  6 ARA   ARA01_20220111…      0.622                     3          0.25  positi…
#>  7 ARA   ARA01_20220111…      0.908                     1          0.167 not_re…
#>  8 ARA   ARA01_20220115…      0.552                     4          0.167 positi…
#>  9 ARA   ARA01_20220115…      0.964                     4          0.167 positi…
#> 10 ARA   ARA01_20220115…      0.723                     4          0.167 positi…
#> 11 ARA   ARA01_20220115…      0.576                     4          0.167 negati…
#> 12 ARA   ARA01_20220115…      0.705                     1          0.333 positi…

They come from a "random_detections" run (occasion = file, threshold 0.5) on simulated data (data-raw/make_extdata.R).

Occasion

An occasion is the sampling unit of the occupancy model, set by occasion_unit:

  • "file": one recording. occasion_id is the file name without extension, e.g. ARA01_20220110_193000.
  • "minute": one minute of a recording, from file_offset. occasion_id is <file>_m<minute>, with the minute zero-based and padded to three digits, e.g. ARA01_20220110_193000_m002 for 120-180 s.

The site, species and occasion (site, species_code, occasion_id) identify the detection history cell. With minute occasions, match them to the occasions of the model by file and minute of clip_start.

clip_manifest.csv

One row per clip. Columns, in this order:

column type definition
site character Site: the folder of the selection table, without the output_ prefix.
species_code character Classifier label, e.g. Boana raniceps_boa-ran.
species_folder character Short species code used as folder name, e.g. boa_ran.
recording_date character YYYYMMDD Date in the recording file name.
night character YYYYMMDD Grouping date: equals recording_date, or the day before for small hours when the hour window crosses midnight.
recording_hour character HH Hour in the recording file name.
rank integer "top": rank by confidence in the site x species x night x hour stratum. "random_detections": order of the clip in its occasion (by file_offset). NA in "random_recordings".
confidence double BirdNET confidence score. NA for whole-recording clips ("random_recordings").
clip_file character File name of the clip (<conf>_<rank>_<recording>_<start>s_<end>s.wav, or rec_<site>_<species>_<occasion_id>.wav for whole recordings).
clip_start, clip_end double (s) Start and end of the clip in the source recording. clip_end is NA for whole recordings of unknown length.
duration double (s) clip_end - clip_start.
source_audio character Path of the source recording, after remapping.
begin_path character Path as written in the selection table (Begin Path).
status character ok, already_exists, audio_not_found, simulated or error: <message>.
sampling_mode character top, random_detections or random_recordings.
occasion_id character Occasion (see above).
n_detections_occasion integer Predictions of the species with confidence >= threshold in the occasion. NA when no threshold was given.
inclusion_prob double Probability that the occasion (or recording) was drawn. NA in "top", which is not a probability sample.

In "random_detections", every prediction >= threshold of a drawn occasion is cut, so the number of clips of the occasion equals n_detections_occasion. This is the assumption of the observation-confirmation design (Chambert et al. 2015, https://doi.org/10.1890/14-1507.1): every detection of a checked occasion is checked.

validation_by_clip.csv

The manifest plus two columns:

column type definition
verdict character positive (true detection), negative (false positive), not_reviewed (clip found in the review folder, but in no subfolder matching the positive or negative pattern, e.g. still in the species folder) or clip_missing (clip not found in the review folder).
reviewed_path character Path where the reviewed clip was found; NA when missing.

Only positive and negative are reviewed verdicts. Clips of "random_recordings" (confidence = NA) are the second method of a multiple-method design (Miller et al. 2011, https://doi.org/10.1890/10-1396.1), that is, manual annotation of recordings. They are not confirmations of detections and must not go to the validation argument of crywolf::fp_aggregate().

Export for occupancy models

export_occupancy_data() writes in one folder everything an occupancy model with false positives needs: every occasion, the classifier scores, the reviewed clips with their design and, optionally, covariates of the occasions and posterior draws of a Bayesian calibration. The folder follows the schema sheepdog-occupancy, version 1.1, described below. The tables are plain CSV files (missing values are empty cells); the calibration draws are a Parquet file.

ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog")
det <- read_selection_tables(file.path(ex, "birdnet"))
out <- export_occupancy_data(
  file.path(tempdir(), "occupancy"), det,
  recordings = file.path(ex, "recordings.csv"),
  validation = list.files(file.path(ex, "validation"), full.names = TRUE)
)
vapply(out$tables, nrow, integer(1))
#>  occasions detections     scores validation      sites 
#>        354       7553       2298       2467          4

The example clips were drawn with "top", so validation.csv serves the calibration but not the false-positive rate of an occupancy model (see sampling_mode below).

schema.json

field definition
schema, schema_version "sheepdog-occupancy" and 1.1. Minor versions only add tables, columns or fields, so a reader of version 1 can read any 1.x by ignoring what it does not know; it should refuse other names and major versions. Version 1.1 added the occasion covariates and the calibration keys; version 1.2, occasion_draws.parquet.
created, sheepdog_version, classifier Provenance of the export.
occasion_unit "file" or "minute" (see Occasion above).
min_confidence Scores below this value were not written: an occasion x species pair absent from scores.csv had no prediction at or above it.
dawn_hour Recordings before this hour belong to the night before.
sites, species Every site and every classifier label (species_code) of the export.
tables For each table, its file and number of rows.
occasion_covariates The columns of occasions.csv after the fixed ones (from occasion_covariates and the calibration keys), when any.
occasion_draws Written by occasion_draws() (version 1.2): file, rule, p_min (with "threshold"), seed (with "sample"), n_draws and species.
calibration With fit: engine, formula, n_draws, grid_step, grid_min, keys (the columns that identify a row of calibration_draws.parquet within a draw: site, species, the calibration_keys and grid_index) and new_levels ("uncertainty": levels of a key absent from the calibration data are drawn from the distribution of the group).

occasions.csv

One row per occasion, with or without predictions, from the list of recordings (recordings).

column type definition
site, occasion_id character The occasion (see Occasion above).
source_audio character Path of the recording.
recording_date, recording_hour character Date (YYYYMMDD) and hour (HH) in the file name.
night character YYYYMMDD Night of the occasion: the day before for recordings before dawn_hour.
start, duration double (s) Start of the occasion in the recording (0 for files) and its length (NA when unknown).
further columns any Covariates of the occasion from occasion_covariates, and the calibration keys, always written as text (e.g. month, YYYYMM, derived from recording_date when not given).

detections.csv and scores.csv

detections.csv has one row per prediction with confidence >= min_confidence: site, occasion_id, species_code, species (the short code of species_folder, the key of the calibration), file_offset (s) and confidence. scores.csv summarises them by occasion x species: max_score (the highest confidence) and n_above_min (the number of predictions). Pairs absent from scores.csv are censored at min_confidence.

validation.csv and recordings_verified.csv

validation.csv holds the clips of the "top" and "random_detections" designs: site, occasion_id, species_code, species, clip_start, clip_end, confidence, sampling_mode, inclusion_prob, n_detections_occasion, verdict (as in validation_by_clip.csv, or disagreement after consensus_verdicts()) and tp (1 for positive, 0 for negative, empty otherwise), plus reviewer and n_reviewers when present. Only clips of "random_detections" estimate a false-positive rate; "top" clips serve the calibration.

recordings_verified.csv holds the occasions annotated by ear ("random_recordings"), with present (1, 0 or empty) in place of tp. The two tables are kept apart because they say different things: a positive clip proves that the species called in its occasion, a negative clip only that this prediction was false (the species may have called with a lower score), while an annotated recording gives the state of the whole occasion.

sites.csv

One row per site, with the covariates given in sites.

calibration_draws.parquet

With fit (a model of fit_calibration(engine = "brms")), n_draws draws of the posterior of P(TP) on a grid of scores from min_confidence in steps of grid_step, for each site x species with predictions: draw, site, species, one text column per calibration key, grid_index, confidence (the grid point) and p_tp. A detection takes the value of the grid point nearest its score, as in score_detections(), and of the levels of the keys of its occasion in occasions.csv. Every level of a key found among the occasions of a site is covered. Species absent from the calibration are left out; sites and key levels absent from it are drawn as new levels of their group. Reading it needs the ‘arrow’ package (in R) or any Parquet reader.

occasion_draws.parquet

Written into an export by occasion_draws(): for each calibration draw, the detection y of every occasion with at least one prediction of the species (draw, site, occasion_id, species as the short code, y as a 32-bit integer). y is 1 when at least one prediction of the occasion is judged true in that draw, 0 when none is, and empty when the occasion cannot be scored (a prediction without calibration draws). The other occasions of occasions.csv are 0 in every draw. With rule = "sample" a prediction is judged true at random with its probability of being true; with "threshold", when that probability is at least p_min. Fitting the occupancy model to each draw and pooling the posteriors propagates the uncertainty of the calibration (Monte Carlo propagation); crywolf::fp_draws_data() reads the table when its settings match the request and otherwise draws the same detections itself.

occasion_draws(file.path(tempdir(), "occupancy"), rule = "sample",
               n_draws = 50, seed = 2026)

End to end: the Curiango data

This section runs the whole flow, from the classifier scores to the occupancy estimates, on real data: the Common Pauraque (Nyctidromus albicollis) recordings of Piatti et al. (data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21795898; article: https://doi.org/10.1002/jav.03737). The models take hours, so the code below is not run here; the results are read from tables cached in the package, written by dev/benchmarks/curiango-export.R and dev/benchmarks/curiango-flow.R of the source repository.

The recorders took one-minute recordings at four sites; the occasion is the recording (occasion_unit = "file"), grouped into nights at each recorder, the sites of the occupancy model. Two classifiers scored them: a custom one and BirdNET. About 1% of the recordings, drawn in proportion to the effort of each site without looking at the scores, were annotated by ear; each annotated minute with a score is a reviewed clip of the observation-confirmation design, and the calibration is fitted to these clips.

1. Export 

fit <- fit_calibration(val_cal, tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | site), engine = "brms",
                       prior = calibration_prior(tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | site),
                                                 val_cal),
                       chains = 4, iter = 2000, seed = 2026)
export_occupancy_data(
  "curiango/custom", detections, recordings = recordings,
  validation = validation, fit = fit,
  occasion_covariates = covariates, # night_site_id, temp, rh, moon, bio, aci
  min_confidence = 0.1, n_draws = 100, seed = 2026)

The model of the calibration is chosen by cross-validated log-loss among tp ~ logit_conf and tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | site) (custom classifier: with the site; BirdNET: without), and fitted with ‘brms’ with the prior of calibration_prior() (see vignette("bayesian-calibration")).

2. Check the calibration

Before the calibration draws are used, the calibration must reproduce the data it was fitted to: the share of true positives overall, by score bin, by site and by month.

ppc <- calibration_ppc(fit, val_cal, group = "month")
plot_calibration_ppc(ppc, check = "month")
ppc <- flow("ppc")
ppc_n <- aggregate(cbind(groups = 1, flagged = flagged) ~ classifier + check,
                   data = ppc, FUN = sum)
ppc_n[order(ppc_n$classifier, ppc_n$check), ]
#>    classifier   check groups flagged
#> 1     birdnet   month     12       6
#> 3     birdnet overall      1       0
#> 5     birdnet   score      8       0
#> 7     birdnet    site      7       1
#> 9     birdnet species      1       0
#> 2      custom   month     16       6
#> 4      custom overall      1       0
#> 6      custom   score      8       1
#> 8      custom    site      7       0
#> 10     custom species      1       0
month <- ppc[ppc$check == "month" & ppc$flagged,
             c("classifier", "group", "n", "observed", "pred_mean", "p_value")]
month[4:6] <- lapply(month[4:6], round, 3)
month
#>    classifier  group   n observed pred_mean p_value
#> 18     custom 202311  24    0.625     0.394   0.001
#> 19     custom 202312  86    0.035     0.149   1.000
#> 20     custom 202401 110    0.009     0.117   1.000
#> 21     custom 202402  24    0.000     0.097   0.958
#> 25     custom 202406 130    0.854     0.738   0.000
#> 28     custom 202409  22    0.591     0.432   0.034
#> 51    birdnet 202311  11    1.000     0.765   0.028
#> 53    birdnet 202401   5    0.000     0.771   0.999
#> 54    birdnet 202403  26    0.654     0.860   0.993
#> 57    birdnet 202406 116    0.940     0.866   0.012
#> 58    birdnet 202407  20    0.700     0.867   0.971
#> 61    birdnet 202410  39    1.000     0.838   0.001
plot_calibration_ppc(ppc, check = "month") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ classifier, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x")

Both calibrations reproduce the overall share of true positives, but not the share by month: in some months nearly every reviewed minute was a true detection, in others almost none, beyond what the score predicts. The probability that a prediction is true depends on how much the species called that month, which a calibration on the score alone (and the site) does not see. The draws below inherit this misfit. A calibration with the month (tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | month), exported with calibration_keys = "month") removes it, but the month then carries calling activity into P(TP), and the reviewed minutes inform both the calibration and the occupancy model; it is a sensitivity analysis here, not the recommended model.

3. Versions of the detections 

occasion_draws("curiango/custom", rule = "sample", n_draws = 20, seed = 2026)

Each version is one draw of which predictions are true; an occasion is a detection when at least one of its predictions is. The share of minutes with a detection per version:

versions <- flow("versions")
aggregate(detection_rate ~ classifier, data = versions,
          FUN = function(x) round(c(mean = mean(x), min = min(x), max = max(x)), 4))
#>   classifier detection_rate.mean detection_rate.min detection_rate.max
#> 1    birdnet              0.0585             0.0553             0.0614
#> 2     custom              0.0785             0.0652             0.0949

4. Occupancy in crywolf

crywolf reads the export, takes the versions from occasion_draws.parquet (its fp_draws_data() draws the same ones when the table is absent), fits the occupancy model with false positives to each version and pools the posteriors in equal shares.

x <- crywolf::fp_read_sheepdog("curiango/custom", species = "nyc_alb")
versions <- crywolf::fp_draws_data(x, rule = "sample", n_draws = 20,
                                   seed = 2026, occasions = occ, sites = nights,
                                   site = "night_site_id")
mc <- crywolf::fp_occu_mc(versions, occ = ~ temp + rh + moon,
                          det = ~ bio + aci, fp = ~ 1, seed = 1,
                          parallel = TRUE)
summary(mc)

occ holds the minute covariates (bio, aci) and nights the night covariates (temp, rh, moon), all standardised.

fits <- flow("fits")
aggregate(cbind(fits = 1, kept = kept, divergences = divergences) ~ classifier,
          data = fits, FUN = sum)
#>   classifier fits kept divergences
#> 1    birdnet   20   20           0
#> 2     custom   20   20           0
s <- flow("summary")
s <- s[grepl("^occ_|^p10_ref$|^p11_ref$", s$variable),
       c("classifier", "variable", "mean", "sd", "sd_within", "sd_between",
         "share_between")]
s[-1:-2] <- lapply(s[-1:-2], round, 3)
s
#>    classifier        variable   mean    sd sd_within sd_between share_between
#> 1      custom occ_(Intercept) -1.247 0.163     0.076      0.144         0.783
#> 2      custom        occ_temp -0.047 0.083     0.062      0.056         0.444
#> 3      custom          occ_rh -0.659 0.125     0.067      0.106         0.711
#> 4      custom        occ_moon  0.151 0.082     0.071      0.042         0.261
#> 10     custom         p11_ref  0.172 0.012     0.003      0.011         0.915
#> 13     custom         p10_ref  0.045 0.007     0.001      0.007         0.981
#> 15    birdnet occ_(Intercept) -0.857 0.067     0.062      0.027         0.158
#> 16    birdnet        occ_temp -0.323 0.059     0.056      0.018         0.092
#> 17    birdnet          occ_rh -0.566 0.062     0.059      0.017         0.076
#> 18    birdnet        occ_moon  0.084 0.061     0.060      0.015         0.058
#> 24    birdnet         p11_ref  0.133 0.005     0.003      0.003         0.565
#> 27    birdnet         p10_ref  0.014 0.001     0.001      0.000         0.383

sd_within is the posterior uncertainty given one version of the detections, and sd_between the uncertainty about which detections are true; their squares add up to the pooled variance (share_between is the share of the second). Every fit converged (largest R-hat 1.005, no divergent transitions).

With the custom classifier, most of the posterior variance of the occupancy intercept and of the humidity effect comes from the calibration: which of its many low-scoring predictions are true changes from version to version, and a model fitted to any one version alone would report about half the posterior standard deviation. BirdNET gives few predictions, most of them confident, so its versions differ little and the uncertainty is mostly within each fit. The two classifiers also disagree on the temperature effect; with the misfit of the calibrations by month, this comparison is a demonstration of the flow, not an ecological result.

Files written by v1.2.0

Up to v1.2.0 the same tables were written in Portuguese (manifesto_clipes.csv, validacao_por_clipe.csv). sheepdog reads them and renames on reading. The map is:

v1.2.0 v2.0.0
local site
pasta_especie species_folder
data_gravacao recording_date
noite night
hora_gravacao recording_hour
arquivo_clipe clip_file
inicio_clipe, fim_clipe, duracao clip_start, clip_end, duration
audio_origem source_audio
begin_path_original begin_path
modo_amostragem sampling_mode
ocasiao_id occasion_id
n_deteccoes_ocasiao n_detections_occasion
prob_inclusao inclusion_prob
veredito verdict
caminho_wav reviewed_path

Values: aleatorio_deteccoes and aleatorio_gravacoes become random_detections and random_recordings; positivo, negativo, nao_validado and clipe_ausente become positive, negative, not_reviewed and clip_missing; ja_existia, audio_nao_encontrado, simulado and erro: become already_exists, audio_not_found, simulated and error:. Whole-recording clips cut by v1.2.0 keep their grav_ prefix on disk; new ones use rec_.

Reading the validation in crywolf 

v <- crywolf::fp_read_validation(validation)

fp_read_validation() reads the v1.2.0 format; reading the column names above needs a crywolf version that supports them.
